query: Consider the following context: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent properties such as high strength, good ductility, superior corrosion resistance, and thermal stability, making them highly promising for applications in the aerospace, energy, and automotive industries. Among them, the FeNiCrMn HEA demonstrates outstanding corrosion resistance while eliminating the expensive Co element present in the “Cantor” alloy, significantly reducing costs. However, current research on the FeNiCrMn HEA has primarily focused on its corrosion resistance, with relatively limited studies on its mechanical properties. revised_generation.uncertainty: Processing problems due to high melting point and limited studies on mechanical properties

cited_evidence.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.
We developed high-temperature high-damping high-entropy alloys with superior mechanical properties via Snoek relaxation.
